decisions.evidence: Candidate C1 cites an entry multiple of '26.9x trailing P/E' [L85], which aligns with the calculation in [D159], but then projects a '15% EPS CAGR' [L86] without the specific forward P/E and five-to-ten-year Microsoft multiple range authentication [L159] and erroneously attributes OpenAI equity value as a core valuation driver [L66], whereas the pack explicitly states such valuation details were unavailable for a verified forward multiple [L159].
decisions.fix: Focus exclusively on verified historical financials and avoid over-extrapolating unverified forward multiples or OpenAI's speculative valuation [L159].

decisions.evidence: Candidate C2 projects '15% EPS growth and a terminal multiple of 28x' [L137, L149], which involves predictive modeling not supported by the pack's warning that forward P/E and full multiple ranges were not recovered [L159].
decisions.fix: Remove speculative terminal multiple projections not supported by the data pack [L159].

notes: Both candidates perform well in identifying the core business quality [D156] and the T1 nature of the market dislocation [D159, D160]. They differ from the gold standard primarily by imputing forward valuation metrics (terminal multiples and forward P/E) that the pack explicitly notes were unavailable for authentication as of the Jan 30 cutoff [L159].
